title: Taking a Message
lines: Hello. This is James Wilson from Star Logistics. Could I speak to Mr. Ito?
I'm sorry, but Mr. Ito is in a meeting right now. Can I take a message?
Yes, please. Could you tell him that the shipment will arrive one day late?
Of course. So it will arrive on Thursday instead of Wednesday?
That's right. And please ask him to call me back this afternoon.
Certainly. Could I have your phone number, please?
Thank you, Mr. Wilson. I'll give him the message as soon as he's free.

questions.q: Why can Mr. Ito not take the call?
When will the shipment arrive?

title: Brainstorming Ideas
lines: Our goal today is to find ways to get more young customers. Any idea is welcome.
How about making short videos for social media?
Maybe fun videos that show how people use our products in daily life.
We could also work with student clubs. For example, give free samples at university events.
I like that. It's not expensive, and we can meet students directly.
What if we create a student discount, too?
That might work, but we should check how it affects our profit.
Fair point. Let's list all the ideas and choose the top three next week.
Should we each estimate the cost of one idea?
Yes, that would help a lot. Thanks, everyone.

questions.q: What is the goal of the meeting?
What will they do next week?

title: Explaining a Mistake
scene: 取引先にミスを説明して謝る
lines: Ms. Garcia, thank you for taking my call. I need to apologize for a mistake on our side.
The invoice we sent last week had the wrong amount. We charged you for twelve hundred units instead of one thousand.
I see. I'm glad you noticed before we paid.
We're very sorry. I'll send a corrected invoice today.
Thank you. How did it happen?
Someone typed the number by hand. We are changing our system so that the numbers come directly from the order.
That sounds like a good fix.
Again, I'm sorry for the trouble. Please let me know if you have any questions.
Thanks for being honest about it, Shin.

questions.q: What was wrong with the invoice?
How will they prevent this mistake in the future?
options: Take numbers directly from the order

title: Asking About a Report
scene: 報告書について質問する
lines: Sakura, I read your report on customer satisfaction. It was very interesting.
Thank you. Did you have any questions?
Yes. On page four, you say satisfaction fell in the summer. What do you think caused that?
We think it was the delivery delays. Many complaints in July were about late deliveries.
That makes sense. How many customers answered the survey?
About two thousand, so the results are quite reliable.
Great. And what do you recommend we do?
First, give customers clear delivery dates. Second, send a message when there's a delay.
Both sound easy to do. Could you present this at the team meeting next week?

questions.q: What probably caused satisfaction to fall in the summer?
How many customers answered the survey?

title: Taking a Day Off
lines: Ms. White, could I take next Friday off?
Next Friday? Let me check the schedule.
My sister is getting married, and the wedding is in Hokkaido.
Congratulations to her! Friday should be fine. Is anything due that day?
The weekly report, but I can finish it on Thursday.
Good. And who will answer your customer emails?
I've asked Aya. She agreed to check them for me.
Perfect. Please set an out-of-office message, too.
I will. Thank you very much.

questions.q: Why does Kaito want Friday off?
Who will check Kaito's customer emails?

title: Discussing a Budget
scene: 予算について話し合う
lines: Takumi, I've looked at your budget for the marketing event. It's about thirty percent over our plan.
I know. The hall is more expensive this year.
There is one, but it's far from the station. Fewer people may come.
I see. What about other costs? Can anything be reduced?
We could print fewer brochures and use a QR code instead.
Good idea. How much would that save?
About ten percent of the total.
That helps. If you can find another ten percent, I can approve it.
Let me talk to the catering company. Maybe we can choose a simpler menu.
Great. Please send me the new numbers by Wednesday.

questions.q: Why is the budget higher this year?
How will Takumi save money on brochures?
options: Print fewer and use a QR code

title: Welcoming a Visitor
lines: Good morning, Mr. Lopez. Welcome to our office. I'm Mayu Kato.
Good morning. Thank you for having me.
Yes, your directions were very clear.
I'm glad. May I take your coat?
The meeting room is this way. Would you like something to drink? Coffee, tea, or water?
Green tea would be lovely, if you have it.
Of course. Please have a seat. Mr. Yamada will join us in a few minutes.
No problem. What a great view from here!
Yes, on a clear day you can see Mount Fuji.

questions.q: What does Mr. Lopez want to drink?
What can you see from the room on a clear day?

title: A Team Disagreement
scene: チーム内の意見の対立
lines: I think we should launch the new app in March. Our competitors are moving fast.
I understand, but the app still has too many bugs. If we launch too early, users will leave.
But if we wait until June, we might lose the market.
You both have good points. Laura, how many serious bugs are there?
About fifteen. Five of them could cause users to lose data.
Those five must be fixed before any launch. How long would that take?
Then here's an idea. Fix the five serious bugs, and launch a test version for a small group in April.
That way we can still move early and get feedback.
And we won't risk all our users. I can agree with that.

questions.q: Why does Laura want to wait?
options: The app has too many bugs

questions.q: What does the manager suggest?
options: Fix serious bugs and launch a test version in April

title: Asking for Directions
lines: Excuse me. Could you tell me how to get to the Lincoln Building?
Sure. Go straight down this street for two blocks.
Then turn left at the bank. The Lincoln Building is the tall glass building on your right.
How long does it take to walk there?
About ten minutes. Or you can take the number 5 bus.
I think I'll walk. I have some time before my meeting.
Thank you so much for your help.

questions.q: Where should Hiro turn left?
How will Hiro go to the building?

title: Following Up After a Meeting
scene: 商談の後のお礼と確認
lines: Mr. Kim, thank you again for meeting us yesterday.
It was a pleasure. Your proposal was very interesting.
I'm glad to hear that. I wanted to confirm the next steps.
We'll send you a sample of the product by next Friday. Then your team will test it for two weeks.
That's right. And after the test, we'll give you our feedback.
Perfect. Is there anything else you need from us?
Could you also send some information about your delivery times to Korea?
Certainly. I'll include that with the sample.
Thank you. I look forward to working with you.

questions.q: How long will Mr. Kim's team test the sample?
What extra information does Mr. Kim ask for?

title: Training a New Employee
lines: Sota, today I'll show you how to handle customer orders.
First, when an order comes in, check that the product is in stock.
In this system. Type the product number here, and you'll see the inventory.
I see. What if it's out of stock?
Then email the customer and tell them the expected date. Never leave them waiting without information.
Got it. And if it is in stock?
Confirm the order, and the warehouse will ship it the same day.
That sounds simple. Can I try the next one myself?
Sure. I'll watch and help if you need it.

questions.q: What should Sota check first when an order comes in?
options: That the product is in stock

questions.q: What should Sota do if a product is out of stock?
options: Email the customer with the expected date

title: Talking About Career Goals
scene: 上司とキャリアについて話す
lines: Riku, where would you like to be in three years?
I'd like to lead a small team, maybe in international sales.
That's a clear goal. What skills do you think you need?
Better English, especially for negotiations. And more experience managing projects.
Good. There's a project with our partner in Australia starting next month. Would you like to join?
You'd be in charge of the weekly calls with their team.
That would be great practice. Thank you for the chance.
Let's check how it's going every two months.
Sounds good. I'll do my best.

questions.q: What does Riku want to do in three years?
What will Riku be in charge of in the new project?
options: The weekly calls with the partner's team

title: Returning a Product
lines: Hi, I'd like to return this jacket. I bought it last Saturday.
Sure. Is there something wrong with it?
No, it's just too small. Do you have it in a larger size?
Let me check. I'm sorry, the large is sold out in this color.
Oh, that's a shame. What other colors do you have?
We have it in dark blue and gray in a large.
The fitting room is over there.
This one fits perfectly. Can I exchange it?
Of course. Since it's the same price, there's nothing more to pay.

questions.q: Why does the customer want to return the jacket?
options: She does not like the color

questions.q: Which color does she choose in the end?

title: Planning a Business Trip
lines: Mr. Mori, I'm booking your trip to Berlin. When would you like to leave?
The conference starts on the twelfth, so I'd like to arrive the day before.
There's a direct flight on the eleventh that arrives at six in the evening.
And for the hotel, would you like one near the conference center?
Yes, within walking distance if possible.
There's one five minutes away. It's a little expensive, but it's within the company's limit.
That's fine. And I'll need to come back on the fifteenth.
OK. I'll send you all the details by email today.

questions.q: When does the conference start?
What kind of hotel does Mr. Mori want?
options: One within walking distance of the conference center

title: Answering Questions After a Presentation
lines: That's the end of my presentation. Does anyone have any questions?
Yes. You said costs will fall by fifteen percent. How did you calculate that?
Good question. It's based on a test we did in two factories over six months.
Will it work in all of our factories?
Not exactly. Older factories may see smaller savings, maybe around ten percent.
And how much will the new system cost?
I don't have the exact number with me. Can I email it to you this afternoon?
Thank you. Any other questions? If not, thank you all for listening.

questions.q: How did Yoko calculate the fifteen percent?
options: From a test in two factories

questions.q: What does Yoko do when she does not know the cost?
options: She offers to email it later

title: Renewing a Contract
lines: Haruka, our contract ends next month. Are you planning to renew it?
We'd like to, but we have a few requests.
First, we'd like faster support. Sometimes we waited two days for an answer.
I'm sorry about that. We can offer support within four hours for your account.
That would help a lot. Second, we'd like to keep the same price for two years.
If you sign a two-year contract, we can keep the price the same.
That sounds fair. Could you send a draft of the new contract?
I'll send it by Friday. Please check it with your legal team.
Will do. Thanks for being flexible.

questions.q: What was Haruka's first request?
What is needed to keep the same price?

title: Dinner with a Client
lines: Thank you for inviting me to such a nice restaurant, Kana.
It's our pleasure. Have you tried Japanese food like this before?
Only sushi in London. This is my first time trying tempura in Japan.
I hope you enjoy it. This restaurant is famous for its fresh vegetables.
It's delicious. How long have you worked with your company?
About six years. I started in the finance team and moved to sales two years ago.
Interesting. Which do you like better?
Sales, I think. I enjoy meeting people like you.
That's very kind. Next time you come to London, dinner is on me.

questions.q: What is Mr. Evans trying for the first time in Japan?
Which team did Kana start in?

title: Ending a Project
scene: プロジェクトの振り返り
lines: The project is finished. Let's look back. What went well?
We finished on time, and the client was very happy with the result.
I think our daily fifteen-minute meetings helped a lot. Everyone knew what others were doing.
Agreed. And what could we do better next time?
We spent too much time on the first design. We should show the client simple drafts earlier.
Also, the testing was rushed at the end. We need more time for it in the plan.
Good points. So next time: show drafts early and plan more time for testing.
Should we write this down for other teams?
Yes. I'll share a short summary with the department.
Thanks, everyone. It was a great team.

questions.q: What helped the team, according to Jack?
What will they do differently next time?
options: Show drafts early and plan more time for testing
